kinds.a: meal shake · complete food · drinkable meal · meal-replacement powder · diet shake
kinds.d: Powder or ready-to-drink shake made to replace a whole meal with set calories and nutrients.

kinds.a: ONS · sip feed · nutritional drink · supplement drink · complete nutrition drink
kinds.d: Energy- and nutrient-dense drink or powder taken alongside food when appetite or diet falls short, often under medical advice.

kinds.a: hypoallergenic formula · amino-acid formula · elemental formula · metabolic formula · food for special medical purposes · medical food
kinds.d: Formula made for the dietary management of a medical condition, such as allergy or a metabolic disorder; a food, not a supplement.

brands.d: Hertfordshire maker of nutritionally complete powders, founded by Julian Hearn with nutritionist James Collier.
Los Angeles meal-replacement brand of Soylent Nutrition, sold as powder and ready-to-drink; now owned by Starco Brands.
Munich maker of bottled drinkable meals, founded by Noel Bollmann and Benjamin Kremer; also powders and bars.
Diet shake and bar brand launched by Thompson Medical Company; later owned by Unilever, Glanbia and Heartland Food Products Group.
Illinois healthcare group whose nutrition arm makes Ensure, Glucerna, Similac and PediaSure.
Dutch specialised-nutrition company, part of Danone since 2007, making medical nutrition and infant formula.
Evansville, Indiana nutrition company best known for Enfamil; part of Reckitt.
Powdered milk drink launched by Glaxo as 'the complete planned food'; Complan Foods, owned by Danone, and by Zydus Wellness in India.
Nestlé nutrition unit whose BOOST line covers oral nutritional supplements.

notes: All three planned kinds kept. Meal-replacement shake: Huel SKUs cut from 4 to 2 (Huel Essential and Superblend dropped as near-duplicates) and Huel range entry dropped; Soylent, yfood and SlimFast added. yfood is listed as a generic ready-to-drink meal because its site names flavours, not a model line. Oral nutritional supplement is a new kind (Ensure, Glucerna, Fortisip Compact, BOOST, Complan). Medical-condition formula stays kind-level with Mead Johnson, Nutricia (Neocate) and Abbott (EleCare). Fortisip variants named only in search snippets (Compact Protein, Compact Fibre) left out; Nestlé Health Science founding year and country not on a retrieved page, so left blank. Tier shelf: no archetypes or traditions.
